title: Coffee Disturbs Sleep in Ways We May Not Notice
paragraphs: Many people drink coffee every day, and some say it does not affect their sleep at all. However, a new scientific review suggests that caffeine may change how the brain sleeps, even when people feel that they have slept well.

The review was written by J. Chmiel and Donata Kurpas, researchers from universities in Poland, including Wroclaw Medical University. It was published in the journal Nutrients in 2026. The researchers looked at 32 studies that used EEG, a method that records the brain's electrical activity, to study the effects of caffeine on sleep.

According to the review, caffeine may reduce "slow-wave activity," which is a sign of deep, restful sleep. At the same time, it may increase faster brain waves that are linked to being awake. This means that even if people sleep for a normal amount of time, their brains may not rest as fully.
Some of the studies found that caffeine still disturbed sleep when people drank it six hours before going to bed. One study even found effects 12 hours later.

Interestingly, people often do not notice these changes. They may fall asleep easily and not remember waking up during the night. However, the EEG may still show less deep sleep. According to Kurpas, feeling that you slept well does not always match what the brain recordings show. People who drink coffee regularly were especially bad at noticing the difference.

Kurpas also warned that poor sleep can lead to a cycle of more tiredness, more need for caffeine and even worse sleep. However, Kurpas said that caffeine is neither "good" nor "bad," and its effects depend on the amount, the time of day and the person.
Not all research agrees. A large study from Sweden in 2026 suggested that coffee may have less effect on sleep than many people believe.
